pr_title: drivers: pinmux stm32F1 remap AFIO without changing the SWJ_CFG
pr_body:
Change the SPI1_REMAP bit of the AFIO_MAPR of the stm32F1x soc
without changing the SWJ_CFG[2:0]: Serial wire JTAG configuration

fix https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38354

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu <francois.ramu@st.com>
pr_comments:
OK, 
going to change all remap bits of the AFIO_MAPR register,
It takes the same formula as the LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_xxx without changing the AFIO_MAPR_SWJ_CFG bits.
Remapping on the AFIO_MAPR2 is not to change (LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_xxx does not set the AFIO_MAPR_SWJ_CFG bits)
+ disable clock after AFIO setting

In the stm32F1x, AF remap and debug I/O configuration register (AFIO_MAPR) cannot read the SWJ_CFG bits. The modify register macro must apply the Serial wire JTAG configuration from the CONFIG and not from the MAPR register content.
This new version  is redefining enable/disable remap macro depending on the the CONFIG_GPIO_STM32_SWJ_xxx position
and not from the MAPR register.
@ck-telecom, can you review, or at least test and see if fixes your issue ?
SPI1 remap works well with CONFIG_GPIO_STM32_SWJ_NOJTAG=y

issue_context.title: stm32: stm32f10x JTAG realated gpio repmap didn't works
issue_context.body:
For stm32f103 series when remap JTAG related GPIO for SPI1 function, it seems didn't works

The pinmux driver seems to need disable JTAG enable SWD and enable RCC->APB2ENR clocks which related gpio port
comments:
@ck-telecom  Could you please detail the error you are  seeing and the sequence you are applying 
Based on the stm32f103 datasheet pins, for the SPI1 are mapped on the PA4, PA5, PA6, PA7

@ck-telecom thanks for the details. Let me see if I understood correctly.
The pin configuration used in your SW is in conflict with SWJ default config (mapped on PA13/PA14/PB3/PB4).
So you need a way to remap these pins using AFIO_MAPR(SWJ_CFG[2:0]). Is that correct ?

If yes, then this could be implemented as a specific additional static configuration.
I don't see any easy way to implement this using device tree, so I propose to introduce a dedicated Kconfig symbol:
CONFIG_STM32_REMAP_SWJ_FULL
CONFIG_STM32_REMAP_SWJ_FULL_NO_NJTRST
CONFIG_STM32_REMAP_SWJ_NO_JTAG
CONFIG_STM32_REMAP_SWJ_NO_JTAG_NO_SWJ

Would it work for you ?

@erwango Yes I think it should be work, and just NOTE the stm32f10x errata http://www.st.com/content/ccc/resource/technical/document/errata_sheet/7d/02/75/64/17/fc/4d/fd/CD00190234.pdf/files/CD00190234.pdf/jcr:content/translations/en.CD00190234.pdf SPI1 remap with I2C1 conflict each other

> @erwango Yes I think it should be work, and just NOTE the stm32f10x errata 

Ok, we'll take care to implement this.

> http://www.st.com/content/ccc/resource/technical/document/errata_sheet/7d/02/75/64/17/fc/4d/fd/CD00190234.pdf/files/CD00190234.pdf/jcr:content/translations/en.CD00190234.pdf SPI1 remap with I2C1 conflict each other

Ok, thanks for the heads up but there is nothing we can do for that.
This should be taken care by users when configuring/designing their device.

However, the pins which are possibly conflicting are: PA15 : SPI_NSS or JTDI PB3 : SPI1_SCK or JTDO PB4 : SPI1_MISO or JNTRST PB5 : SPI1 MISO or I2C1_SMBAI Could we introduce a single flag to select the JTag (= MAIN) or not (=DEFAULT or REMAP) for PA15, PB3, PB4 globally (something like _CONFIG_SWJ_NO_REMAP_ or _CONFIG_REMAP_SWJ_PINS_ON_SPI1_) or should have each pin flexible pin assignement. I think the question of PB15 should be handled separately. In your case, because you are using the SPI1_MISO on PB5 (alternate function), the remap applies and consequently the I2C1 must not be clocked, according to the Errata sheet. --> could this be done with `status = "disabled";` directly in your DTS ? On the other side, there is no reason to have ``` &i2c1 { pinctrl-0 = <&i2c1_scl_pb8 &i2c1_sda_pb9>; status = "disabled"; ``` in the _./boards/arm/nucleo_f103rb/nucleo_f103rb.dts_, because the PB5 is not used there (the errata does not apply).

It appears that for the STM32F1x soc series, it already exists in the _./drivers/gpio/gpio_stm32.c_

Could you try to set **CONFIG_GPIO_STM32_SWJ_NOJTAG=y** in your  boards _defconfig
--> _released PB4 PB3 PA15_
but when SPI1 remaped in LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_SPI1(), the LL library LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_SPI1() API set CONFIG_SWJ_NO_REMAP status

yes, so you need 

- to LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_SPI1  --> remap SPI1 (SPI1_REMAP = 1) on SPI1_NSS  PA15,  SPI1_SCK  PB3, SPI1_MISO  PB4, SPI1_MOSI  PB5

- and  LL_GPIO_AF_Remap_SWJ_NOJTAG() --> set the SWJ_CFG[2:0] = 010: JTAG-DP Disabled and SW-DP Enabled which  frees pin PA15, PB3, PB4

The order of the sequence should not change the position of the AFIO_MAPR register. The reason why LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_SPI1 is _also_ setting SWJ _CFG = 111 (which should have 'no effect' on the Serial wire JTAG configuration) is not clear.

with this patch, trying to change only the SPI1_REMAP bit (not SWJ _CFG)  when remapping the SPI1
Changing the SWJ _CFG is done by the `gpio_stm32_afio_init()` function

review_comments: this is a _partial_ remap on 2-bit  TIM3_REMAP[1:0]   (disable_remap is  for 1-bit like SPI1_REMAP or I2C1_REMAP)
